name: Taiga Forest Products Lumber Treatment Facility

commitments.text: Prior to commencement of construction activities Taiga must prepare a schedule for groundwater monitoring and sampling of runoff and provide this schedule to Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks (MELP) and Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) for review and approval.

Prior to commencement of construction activities Taiga must adhere to the sediment and erosion control measures outlined in the MELP/DFO 'Land Development Guidelines For the Protection of Aquatic Habitat' and include these measures as part of a sediment control plan submitted to DFO for review and approval.

Prior to commencement of construction activities Taiga must convene a pre-construction meeting between the Environmental Monitor selected by Taiga and the contractor to ensure that the conditions of the sediment control plan are understood.
Taiga must refrain from any site clearing activities between April 1 and July 31 during any of the years required for construction of the new facility.
Taiga must ensure that no runoff from the treated wood storage area enters local storm sewer systems or creeks.
Taiga must ensure that the quantity of any discharge to the sanitary sewer system meets the sanitary discharge criteria established by the Township of Langley.

Taiga must ensure that the quality of any discharge to the sanitary sewer system meets effluent requirements of the Greater Vancouver Regional District and/or James treatment plant and any applicable Waste Management Permit held by the Township of Langley.
